rv.q: It isn’t groundbreaking but it all makes for a lovely afternoon.
Original it might not be, but a talented cast and a visually stunning sense of spectacle means this hits all the right notes for a festive panto.
It is more of an aesthetic triumph than a fully blown celebration of panto spirit, then.
If you are going to go to a panto this year, I highly suggest that you put Cinderella at the top of your list.
I would definitely recommend a visit to Hammersmith, or 'Glamoursmith' as it's known in the show, to see Cinderella this festive season.
The production sparkles from the moment Ashh Blackwood exuberantly steps on the stage as Buttons, and under Belfield’s nifty direction this version of Cinderella bounces along.

cn.t: Critics find this Cinderella serviceable but uneven, with scene-stealing supporting performances brightening an otherwise safe retelling that doesn't fully deliver the magic it promises.
